source_text: Incola ego sum apud te et peregrinus sicut omnes patres mei. Remitte mihi ut refrigerer priusquam abeam. Gloria Christo Iesu in saecula. Amen.
orientation: Origen closes the homily by quoting the psalmist's final prayer, then adds a doxology to Christ Jesus.
pass_a_gloss: A sojourner I am with you and a pilgrim, just as all my fathers. Forgive me, so that I may be refreshed before I depart. Glory to Christ Jesus forever. Amen.

choices.term: Incola ego sum apud te et peregrinus
choices.english: A sojourner I am with you and a pilgrim
choices.why: Keeps the psalmist's self-description as incola and peregrinus, matching the glossary terms sojourner and pilgrim, and preserves the word order emphasis on the speaker's status.
rejected: I am a resident alien and a stranger with you

choices.why: Remitte is a direct imperative of request; 'forgive' captures the plea for remission of sins in this final prayer.

choices.english: so that I may be refreshed
choices.why: The purpose clause with subjunctive expresses the desired result of forgiveness; 'be refreshed' conveys the cooling relief the psalmist seeks.
rejected: so that I may cool down

choices.why: Priusquam with subjunctive marks the time limit of the request; 'depart' renders abeam as leaving this life, fitting the pilgrim context.
The doxology formula gives glory to Christ Jesus; 'forever' renders in saecula as unending ages, the standard liturgical close.
rejected: Glory to Christ Jesus unto the ages
Glory be to Christ Jesus for ever and ever

pass_b_english: “I am a sojourner with you and a pilgrim, like all my fathers. Forgive me, so that I may be refreshed before I depart” (Psalm 39:12–13, LXX 38:13–14). Glory to Christ Jesus forever. Amen.
